reforms.description: Japan implemented a Science and Technology Basic Plan (decided in 1996) allocating 17.2 trillion yen over five years to R&D, aiming to increase R&D spending toward OECD average levels. The plan boosted budgetary allocation for science and technology in FY2000 as the final year of this five-year plan to strengthen basic R&D capacity. A new competitive scheme for allocating project funds was introduced, though its share remained below 10% compared to higher shares in the US and UK. Japan increased emphasis on basic research and improved efficiency of public technology spending through ongoing efforts to make the system more flexible, competitive and open.
reforms.component_name: Five-year R&D allocation and competitive project funding scheme
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D funding and introduction of competitive allocation mechanisms enhance research capacity and allocative efficiency, supporting long-term productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Plan was decided in 1996 and implemented through FY2000; described as implemented in multiple entries.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural, system-wide reform establishing a major five-year R&D investment programme with 17.2 trillion yen allocation and introduction of competitive funding mechanisms.
reforms.source_quote: Following the Science and Technology Basic Plan (decided in 1996), the government allocated 17.2 trillion yen in total to R&D for five years up to FY2000, aiming to lift its share toward the OECD average.

reforms.description: Japan reformed its intellectual property regime for government-sponsored R&D to enable better commercialisation of publicly funded research. A patent law revision accorded researchers intellectual property rights on government-sponsored research. Additionally, Japan introduced a scheme granting 100 per cent patent rights to private companies for government-sponsored R&D projects, implemented by MITI across 1,111 projects in FY1999 covering 256 billion yen in expenditures.
reforms.package_name: IP Rights Reform for Government-Sponsored R&D
reforms.component_name: 100% patent rights scheme for government-sponsored R&D
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Granting IP rights to researchers and private companies incentivises commercialisation of publicly funded R&D, improving knowledge transfer and innovation outcomes.
reforms.status_evidence: MITI scheme implemented across 1,111 projects in FY1999; patent law revision described as implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant reform of IP regime affecting commercialisation of government-sponsored R&D, with concrete implementation across over 1,000 projects and 256 billion yen in expenditures.
reforms.source_quote: Another scheme seeks to encourage R&D through granting 100 per cent patent rights to private companies for projects sponsored by the government. MITI has applied this principle to all the projects it has granted since the implementation of the law (1111 cases in FY1999 covering expenditures of 256 billion yen).

reforms.description: Japan encouraged more start-ups and venture business through numerous tax and lending programmes introduced since the November 1998 Emergency Economic Measures. However, programmes were assessed as lacking focus and venture finance remained less of a problem than venture firm effectiveness.
reforms.component_name: Tax and lending programmes for start-ups and venture business
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Tax and lending programmes support startup creation and growth, which can enhance innovation and productivity. However, assessment notes lack of focus and effectiveness issues, suggesting mixed or limited actual impact on growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Programmes introduced since November 1998 Emergency Economic Measures; described as implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant policy initiative introducing multiple tax and lending programmes for startup support, though effectiveness was questioned.
reforms.source_quote: Encourage more start-ups and venture business. Numerous tax and lending programmes since the November 1998 Emergency Economic Measures. Programmes lacking focus. Venture finance less of a problem than before but venture firms not effective.

reforms.description: The mid-term review of the Science and Technology Basic Plan (April 1999) identified the need for improved evaluation systems to support more extensive use of competitive project funding schemes in R&D allocation. The review highlighted that evaluation practices were lax, with audit findings showing delays in research reporting and continued funding of underperforming projects.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improved evaluation systems and more competitive allocation of R&D funds enhance allocative efficiency and research quality, supporting productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Mid-term review announced in April 1999 identifying needs for reform; status is announced rather than implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant governance reform addressing evaluation practices and competitive funding mechanisms, though narrower in scope than the main Basic Plan.
reforms.source_quote: The mid-term review of the Basic Plan (April 1999) pointed out that an improved evaluation system would be essential for a more extensive use of the new scheme. Indeed, evaluation in this area seems lax.
